# 8 Essential Dog Grooming Marketing Strategies

By [Hibu](https://hibu.com/blog/authors/hibu) | January 14, 2025

*   [facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies&src=sdkpreparse)

*   [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=false&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies)
*   [Linkedin](mailto:?subject=8%20Essential%20Dog%20Grooming%20Marketing%20Strategies&body=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies)

As the owner of a local dog grooming business, you know how important pets are to their people, and the numbers support this. [According to a 2023 Pew Research Center survey, 97% of US households view pets as family members.](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/pet-grooming-boarding/1735/) This means keeping them happy, healthy, and looking great is often a top priority. Of course, that’s where you and your business come in.

Currently, [the global pet grooming market is worth over $1.3 billion a year](https://www.dogster.com/lifestyle/pet-grooming-industry-statistics), and it’s only expected to grow. With the rise in pet humanization, an increase in busy lifestyles, and the growth of multi-pet households, pet owners have become more and more willing to pay top prices for the best pet care—and, when they’re searching for that best-in-class care, you want them to choose your business specifically to spend their money.

But how do you do that?

**It all comes down to how you market your services**. We can assume that your expertise is in dog _grooming_, not dog _grooming marketing_. So, we’re more than happy to step in on that front–starting with these eight essential dog grooming marketing strategies that you need to know for your local grooming business.

###   
Eight Dog Grooming Marketing Strategies

The right marketing strategies will ensure that pet owners in your local area will be able to find your business and then book your services. The eight we’ll cover here are the most essential ones, so you’ll want to focus on them first.

#### 1\. Optimize your Google listing

Your Google Business listing helps customers in your area find your business when they search for things like “dog grooming near me.” Keeping your profile optimized is crucial for driving traffic to your business. Keep these tips in mind:

*   **Complete your listing:** ensure your address, phone number, email, website, and any other relevant fields are complete and accurate. 
*   **Add photos**: take high-quality photos of the inside and outside of your business, before and after client photos that showcase your skills, and maybe even shots of yourself to add to your profile.
*    **Respond to reviews:** reviews left on Google will appear on your profile and be visible to other potential customers. Whether the reviews are good or bad, you should always take the time to leave at least a quick response.
*   **Keep your profile up to date:** things change, and holidays may affect your hours. When that happens, keep your customers informed by updating your profile. Make sure to also switch out your photos periodically to keep things fresh.   
     

#### 2\. Continually groom your website

Your website is like your business’s digital first impression. You want to make sure it is optimized for mobile, loads quickly, and is free from any mistakes. Similarly to your Google Business Profile, you’ll want to keep it updated with current photos, business hours, and contact information.

Since you run a service business, you’ll also want to include an online booking portal on your site. [Research shows that 90% of customers prefer booking appointments online, and 35% prefer scheduling them during non-business hours](https://calendesk.com/blog/12-reasons-why-you-need-an-online-booking-system-for-small-business). This feature offers convenience for your current customers and prospects and keeps you competitive in the market.

**\[Related:** [5 Things Customers Want to See on Your Local Business Website](https://hibu.com/blog/marketing-tips/5-things-customers-want-to-see-on-your-local-business-website)**\]**

#### 3\. Create grooming packages

Remember how we mentioned that people were living busier lifestyles? That’s where our next strategy comes in. Create pre-made grooming packages to list (with prices!) on your newly polished website. A menu detailing which services their pet will receive will make the booking process much faster and simpler. Plus, you’re the groomer. You know best which services pets need most and which complement each other best.

If you want, you can still create an “a la carte” menu for those customers who only want to purchase one or two of your services. This could even make your packages more desirable if you indicate the discount customers will receive by purchasing the package instead of each service individually.

#### 4\. Set up a customer referral program

Because pet owners love their pets so much, they aren’t always willing to try out new care providers. That is unless the providers come highly recommended by other pet owners. So, encourage your satisfied customers to tell their friends about you with a customer referral program.

A referral program pulls double duty for you. Not only does it help with brand awareness for your business, but it also rewards your loyal customers. [Studies show that customer acquisitions through referrals spend 200% more than the average customer](https://www.annexcloud.com/blog/42-referral-marketing-statistics-that-will-make-you-want-to-start-a-raf-program-tomorrow/).

From discounts on services for every customer referred to free gifts, the possibilities for how to reward your referrals are endless.

#### 5\. Ask for reviews

In the same vein as customer referrals, reviews are essential for dog grooming businesses. Just as people turn to their friends to discover safe places to care for their pets, they also head to the internet. When they do, you’ll want to ensure your reviews put you ahead of the competition.

Encourage satisfied customers to leave reviews by posting QR codes in your waiting room, emailing them a request after their appointment, or sending a follow-up text message.

# The Role of Social Media and Online Marketing in Growing Your Grooming Business

Oct 23, 2024 | [Pet Grooming Business](https://blog.groomsoft.com/category/pet-grooming-business/)

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Gemini_Generated_Image_jdf15pjdf15pjdf1.jpg "Gemini_Generated_Image_jdf15pjdf15pjdf1")

In today’s digital age, social media and online marketing have become indispensable tools for pet grooming businesses looking to expand their client base and showcase their expertise. This article will explore effective strategies for leveraging these platforms to attract new clients, engage with your audience, and ultimately grow your grooming business.

## Harnessing the Power of Social Media Platforms

Social media platforms offer unique opportunities for groomers to connect with pet owners, showcase their work, and build a strong online presence. Each platform has its own strengths and can play a crucial role in your marketing strategy.

Facebook remains a powerful tool for building community and engaging with local clients. Its versatility allows you to share a variety of content, from detailed posts to photos and videos. Facebook’s events feature is particularly useful for promoting special grooming days or workshops. The platform’s robust advertising options also make it easier to target pet owners in your area.

Instagram’s visual nature makes it ideal for showcasing your grooming artistry. Before-and-after photos, grooming process videos, and cute pet pictures can all help attract and engage potential clients. Instagram Stories and Reels offer additional ways to share behind-the-scenes content or quick grooming tips, adding a personal touch to your brand.

TikTok, with its focus on short-form video content, provides an excellent platform for demonstrating your skills in an entertaining way. You can create engaging transformation videos, share fun facts about different breeds, or participate in trending challenges to increase your visibility and appeal to a younger audience of pet owners.

Regardless of which platforms you choose, here are some general tips for effective social media posting:

1.  Consistency is key: Maintain a regular posting schedule to keep your audience engaged and increase your visibility in social media algorithms.
2.  Quality over quantity: While regular posting is important, focus on creating high-quality, valuable content rather than posting for the sake of frequency.
3.  Engage with your audience: Respond to comments, ask questions, and encourage interaction to build a loyal community around your brand.
4.  Use hashtags strategically: Research and use relevant hashtags to increase the discoverability of your posts.
5.  Show your personality: Let your passion for pets and grooming shine through in your posts. Authenticity can help you connect with potential clients on a personal level.
6.  Utilize user-generated content: Encourage clients to share photos of their freshly groomed pets and repost this content (with permission) to build trust and showcase real results.
7.  Stay informed about platform updates: Social media platforms frequently update their features and algorithms. Stay informed to make the most of new opportunities.

By leveraging these platforms effectively and following these general guidelines, you can create a strong social media presence that attracts new clients and reinforces your reputation as a skilled and caring pet groomer.

## Creating Engaging Content

The key to successful social media marketing lies in the quality and relevance of your content. Your posts should be authentic, allowing your personality and passion for pet grooming to shine through. This authenticity helps build trust with your audience and sets you apart from competitors. Education should also be a core component of your content strategy. Share grooming tips, coat care advice, or breed-specific information to position yourself as an expert in your field and provide value to your followers. Consistency in your posting schedule is crucial for maintaining audience engagement and improving your visibility on social media platforms. Finally, make your content interactive by asking questions, running polls, or hosting Q&A sessions. This encourages engagement and helps you build a community around your brand.

Main points for creating engaging content: • Be authentic and showcase your personality • Educate your audience with valuable grooming tips and information • Maintain a consistent posting schedule • Encourage interaction through questions, polls, and Q&A sessions

## Showcasing Your Work

Before-and-after photos are arguably your most powerful marketing tool as a groomer. These visual transformations serve as a testament to your skills and can attract potential clients. When sharing these photos, always ensure you have the pet owner’s permission. Strive for consistency in your photography by using similar lighting conditions for both the “before” and “after” shots. This helps highlight the true transformation. Showcase a variety of breeds, coat types, and grooming styles to demonstrate the breadth of your expertise. Don’t just post the photos – tell a story with them. Use captions to explain the grooming process, highlight specific challenges you overcame, or share interesting facts about the breed or grooming technique used. This additional context adds depth to your posts and further showcases your knowledge and skills.

Key strategies for showcasing your work: • Use high-quality before-and-after photos • Ensure consistency in photography conditions • Display a variety of breeds and grooming styles • Tell the story behind each transformation in your captions

## Leveraging Client Testimonials

Happy clients can be your most effective marketers, and their testimonials can significantly influence potential customers. In the pet grooming industry, where trust and quality of care are paramount, positive reviews from satisfied pet owners can make a substantial difference in attracting new clients.

### The Power of Social Proof

Social proof, in the form of client testimonials, serves as a powerful tool to build credibility and trust with potential clients. When pet owners see others praising your services, they’re more likely to feel confident in choosing your grooming business. This is particularly true in an industry where people are entrusting their beloved pets to your care.

### [What Animal Care and Service Workers Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-2)

Animal care and service workers attend to or train animals.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-3)

Animal care and service workers are employed in a variety of settings, including kennels, zoos, stables, animal shelters, pet stores, veterinary clinics, and aquariums. Some parts of the job may be physically or emotionally demanding, and workers risk injury when caring for animals.

### [How to Become an Animal Care and Service Worker](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-4)

Animal care and service workers typically have a high school diploma or equivalent and learn the occupation on the job. Many employers prefer to hire candidates who have experience working with animals.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-5)

The median annual wage for animal caretakers was $35,360 in May 2025.

The median annual wage for animal trainers was $39,990 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-6)

Overall employment of animal care and service workers is projected to grow 11 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 69,400 openings for animal care and service workers are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

## What Animal Care and Service Workers Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

![Image 1: Animal care and service workers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/images/2698.jpg)

Pet sitters care for pets while the owner is at work or on vacation.

Animal care and service workers attend to or train animals. Working with pets and other nonfarm animals, these caretakers and trainers feed, groom, and exercise the animals or teach them to respond to human commands.

### Duties

Animal care and service workers typically do the following:

*   Give food and water to animals
*   Clean equipment and the living spaces of animals
*   Monitor animals and record details of their diet, physical condition, and behavior
*   Examine animals for signs of illness or injury
*   Exercise animals
*   Bathe animals, trim nails, clip hair, and attend to other grooming needs
*   Train animals to obey or to behave in a specific manner

The following are types of animal care and service workers:

**_Animal trainers_** teach animals a variety of skills, such as obedience, performance, riding, security, and assisting people with disabilities. They familiarize animals with human voices and contact, and they teach animals to respond to commands. Most animal trainers work with dogs and horses, but some work with marine mammals, such as dolphins. Trainers teach a variety of skills.
